criteria.name: Evidence examination and source fidelity
criteria.reason: Credits accurate supplied-exhibit examination and traceability where supported. Evidence analysis says the service corridor provides direct unmonitored access from LAB to EAST CORRIDOR, and conclusion describes V01 as a service-corridor link between those rooms. The actual public plan has the service corridor linked to LAB, with LAB linked separately to EAST CORRIDOR and EAST EXIT. V10 marks the service corridor as blind, not the lab-to-east-corridor connection. This repeated spatial claim changes the inferred route and monitoring coverage. The final narrative still says removal was likely through the service corridor, citing topology and a blind spot without evidence of that actual journey. The source exhibits establish a possible unobserved approach to the lab and an object later at the east exit; an alternative intermediary or route remains a hypothesis, not a preferred observed sequence.

criteria.name: Timeline reconstruction
criteria.reason: Credits recorded chronology and correct incident bounds where present. The report and timeline label the crucial gap 18:00-18:10, while describing it as the gap between the prototype observations at 18:00 and 18:14. The 18:10 corridor snapshot does not show the prototype or establish when it left the lab. Their own deduction correctly gives removal bounds 18:00-18:14, so the labelled interval leaves four minutes unaccounted for. Some suspect-assessment language still places named owners physically at snapshots or calls them not near the lab based on unmapped locations, although surrounding identity and interval caveats are substantially better. The investigation should consistently keep these as inferred associations and refrain from treating absent log entries or one-time locations as a complete opportunity assessment.
